answer: An operator reserves one numbered feed horn on a coastal ocean bluff. Only that holder may bolt a uniquely serialled receiver and, while a published nebula stands in the beam, record a one-shot hydrogen-line tape whose hash must unlock the horn's sealed cipher. Inspectors match feed serial, pointing log, tape hash, and beam clock. A shared horn, a reused receiver, or an off-window recording is forfeited as one farm. Fielding N aliases costs N exclusive horns, N unique receivers, and N live transits no single listener can stack in the same hour.
